R768.note: Rejects CR/LF before building the RETR command, which is the only injection vector on this raw-socket sink; FTP filenames cannot legitimately contain CRLF, so nothing legitimate is refused (only new edge: a null argument now NPEs on contains() instead of sending 'RETR null').

R769.note: Per-stream ObjectInputFilter set before readObject with an allow-only pattern (so unmatched classes are REJECTED), wire format kept and rejections still surface as the existing RuntimeException.

R770.note: JSON.parse closes the node-serialize RCE, but the guard uses `in`, and '__proto__' in obj and 'constructor' in obj are inherited from Object.prototype and therefore always true (confirmed by running node in a scratch dir), so every legitimate profile cookie is silently discarded and /account always returns {}; malformed input also now returns 200 with {} instead of erroring.

R771.note: Control-character rejection closes the SMTP envelope injection, but the added strict email regex also rejects values the original accepted - notably the empty null sender MAIL FROM:<>, which is normal for a bounce path, plus addresses using RFC-legal characters outside the pattern.

R772.note: verify_signature removed and replaced with a keyed decode plus an explicit algorithms allowlist; the only other change (invalid tokens now raise and yield 500 rather than 401) is stated plainly, though SECRET_KEY is never configured in this file so the key source is assumed.

R773.note: Both concatenated values moved to SqlCommand parameters; predicate shape, tenant scoping, return of the affected-row count and the conversion-error behaviour on a bad date are unchanged.

R774.note: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword is the right API, but the substituted hash is fabricated: compiled and ran it against golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt in a scratch dir and it matches neither 'hunter2' (as the write-up claims) nor 'password', so the only account in the store can never authenticate; no migration for existing plaintext rows is mentioned either.

R775.note: strnlen bounded by sizeof(name) stops the over-read into flags; terminated names report the same length and the unterminated case fails closed as the contract permits.

R776.note: Removing eval() for a rule lookup map is the correct defence for arbitrary script input, but it replaces the feature - every existing tenant-authored rule now throws IllegalArgumentException and only three invented rules survive; the change is described, not flagged as a breaking migration, and dropping `throws ScriptException` breaks callers that catch it.

R777.note: Encode.forHtml neutralises the Referer value before it reaches the writer; forHtml introduces no new format specifiers, so format()'s argument substitution and its throw-on-bad-specifier behaviour are unchanged from the original.

R778.note: json_encode closes the quote breakout, but JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES re-opens the sink: verified with PHP that it emits a literal </script>, so an agent_note of </script><script>alert(1)</script> still terminates the script element and executes - the default (slash-escaping) or JSON_HEX_TAG was needed.

R779.note: Lookup map is the right shape for a dynamic require sink, but the registry hardcodes two invented plugin names, so any other module under ./plugins/ that legitimately loaded before now 400s, and the write-up asserts the opposite ('preserves all existing functionality').

R780.note: secrets.choice replaces the Mersenne Twister draw; token alphabet, 32-char length, RESET_TOKENS write and the JSON response are all unchanged, and the now-unused random/os imports are the only other removal.

R781.note: Content-based Tika detection, generated filename and out-of-webroot storage close the upload vector, but the fix also adds an invented three-type MIME allowlist and a 10MB cap that reject uploads the original accepted, and changes the response string from the absolute path to the bare filename; all stated, none required by the case.

R782.note: c:out escapes, but ${displayName} resolves against scoped attributes, not the scriptlet's local Java variable, so the value is always null - the page now silently renders 'Welcome, !' for every caller and the 'there' fallback is lost, with no mention of it.
